clue.text: With this, what I may need becomes themed in a way

definitions.text: With this, what I may need becomes themed in a way

blocks.clueFragment: what I may need becomes themed in a way
blocks.note: surface reading: someone's needs turning into a themed arrangement, like a party plan
setter's reading: the twelve letters of these four words, rearranged, spell out the phrase themed in a way exactly

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a tool that turns their requirements into something with a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-demonstrating: the device it defines is the very device that turns 'what I may need' into 'themed in a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes the wordplay device itself, a rearrangement of letters that converts one phrase into another.

clue.text: Renault coloured grey or beige?

indicators.note: something coloured has been altered in appearance, so the car name's letters are altered in order

blocks.note: the French car maker, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A query about whether a Renault car has been painted in a dull grey or beige.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey and beige are examples of muted, unobtrusive shades, which decorators call neutral colours; the question mark flags definition by example.

clue.text: Stout belly surprisingly empty

indicators.note: emptying a word takes out its insides, leaving only the outside pair of letters

blocks.note: the belly or stomach
first and last letters of surprisingly

explanation.surface: A stout belly that is, oddly, empty, as if a large man has missed lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like a description of the belly; here it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout can mean brave and determined, as in a stout defence, which matches having plenty of courage or nerve.

clue.text: Banff originally in with it, a Canadian province

indicators.note: originally points to how a word starts, so only its opening letter is used
in places one item inside the next one named in the clue

blocks.note: first letter of Banff
being with it means being alert and switched on
taken as written

explanation.surface: Banff, the Rocky Mountain resort town, sits within a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside ALERT, then A follows. Banff really is in Alberta, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of the ten provinces of Canada, lying in the west between British Columbia and Saskatchewan.

clue.text: See 10
See 16 Across
Chap certainly not into flower, strong smeller?

indicators.note: into means the preceding items are put inside the flower word

blocks.note: a rose is a flower
a chap is a man
an emphatic refusal

explanation.surface: A man who is definitely not keen on flowers, though he has a strong sense of smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' could suggest a river, but here it is the bloom; 'strong smeller' is a jokey way to describe a big, bold nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman nose is a prominent, high-bridged nose; the question mark playfully treats a strong-looking nose as an organ for smelling.

clue.text: Piece from electioneer, I established, most weird

indicators.note: a piece from a phrase is a stretch of consecutive letters cut out of it

blocks.note: found running across the end of electioneer, the I, and the start of established

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a political campaigner and something rather strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, so the superlative form matches the weirdest, the most uncanny.

clue.text: Astronomer captures alien for features editor

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: a scientist who studies the universe
the extraterrestrial of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: An astronomer manages to land a job as features editor at a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features editor' reads as a journalist, but the features are facial ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty specialist improves a client's facial features, so jokingly that person edits features rather than newspaper articles.

clue.text: As newlyweds slightly damaged, one trapped

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so the single letter sits within the word for damaged

blocks.note: just as in only just, by a small margin
marred means spoilt or damaged
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Newlyweds are a little damaged, with one of them stuck somewhere, a wedding gone slightly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: One as the Roman numeral I is a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Newlyweds are a couple who have only recently wed, the state proclaimed by the sign on the back of the wedding car.

clue.text: Taxpayer ultimately being squeezed by wretched PM – something alcoholic required!

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so just the final letter of that word is used
a thing squeezed by another is pressed inside it

blocks.note: Theresa May, the British Prime Minister 2016 to 2019, with bloody as a British word for wretched or damned
last letter of taxpayer

explanation.surface: A taxpayer squeezed by an awful Prime Minister needs a stiff drink.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside BLOODY MAY, between MA and Y. Bloody is a mild British swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail of vodka and tomato juice, so it is an alcoholic drink, a classic hangover remedy.

clue.text: Grace perhaps, through catching some light

indicators.note: catching something means holding it within, so one word encloses the other

blocks.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Grace, perhaps a woman's name, shining through as she catches the light.
explanation.walkthrough: Grace looks like a name; it is the thanks said before a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace is the short thanksgiving said before eating, an example of an address to God, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Country ending in recession, many leaving country avoid work

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter, which is all that is taken
when something is leaving, it goes out of the word that held it

blocks.note: the West African country
last letter of recession
taken as written, to be removed
the European country

explanation.surface: A news report on a nation in recession whose people leave rather than work.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking MANY out of GERMANY leaves GER.
explanation.definitionFit: To malinger is to pretend to be ill in order to escape duty or employment, which is shirking one's job.

clue.text: Debunking of fairy tale the cost for conspiracy theorists

indicators.note: debunking a story takes it apart, so the letters of the following words are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: all sixteen letters of these four words

explanation.surface: Exposing a fairy tale comes at a price for people who believe in conspiracies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flat Earth Society is a group that rejects the globe, claiming scientists and governments hide the planet's real shape.

clue.text: Maestro in performing encore lifted up at end of opera

indicators.note: placing something at the end of another means it is attached after it
in a down entry, lifting letters up means reading them from bottom to top

blocks.note: the opera by Puccini
the word in, performing an encore, so given twice

explanation.surface: A conductor in an encore performance is raised up at an opera's conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Arturo Toscanini famously conducted the premieres of several Puccini operas, so Tosca is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Toscanini was the celebrated Italian conductor, and maestro is the honorific for an eminent orchestral leader.

clue.text: Two items of footwear left with everything one’s got

blocks.clueFragment: Two items of footwear left with everything
blocks.note: surface reading: a pair of shoes plus all the rest of one's belongings left behind
setter's reading: an idiom for total commitment, wholeheartedly, read literally as footwear together with everything else

explanation.surface: Someone departs leaving a pair of boots and every other possession.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is chiefly Australian and New Zealand, meaning wholeheartedly; read literally it is footwear plus the rest of one's stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes throwing yourself fully into something, holding nothing back, giving maximum effort and commitment.

clue.text: Flat hand

blocks.note: first meaning: level, even with a surface
second meaning: in poker, five cards all of one suit

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat hand' looks like a palm held out; the words are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means level with a surface, as in fitted flush, and names a poker holding of five same-suit cards.

clue.text: Battle fitting last of scrap into shed

indicators.note: last of a word means only its final letter is kept
fitting something into a structure installs it inside

blocks.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall
last letter of scrap

explanation.surface: A fight that breaks out while fitting the last piece of scrap into a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, chiming with battle, but here it only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto was the 1571 naval engagement in which the Holy League fleet defeated the Ottoman navy off Greece.

clue.text: Real jerks backing legal draft I rejected, undemocratic

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so these letters are read in the opposite direction
jerking something jolts it about, so its letters are jumbled
backing another item means standing behind it, so this piece is placed after

blocks.note: a bill is a draft law put before parliament
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Genuine idiots support a proposed law which I threw out, an unfair, undemocratic affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Illiberal means opposed to freedom of thought and political rights, intolerant of dissent, so it describes undemocratic regimes.

clue.text: Visited by male, I question unwelcome guest

indicators.note: being visited by someone means having them come alongside, so the two pieces sit side by side

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male
a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: A man drops in, and the host wonders about an unwanted visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The I comes first, joined by M, then POSER.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposer is someone who takes unfair advantage of hospitality, foisting themselves on a host, like an intruding houseguest.

clue.text: Princess and I are entwined

indicators.note: things entwined are twisted together, so these letters are intertwined into a new order

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A princess and her lover say they are wrapped up in each other.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariadne gave Theseus a thread to escape the labyrinth, so the twining suits her.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Ariadne was the daughter of King Minos of Crete, so she was royalty by birth.

clue.text: With this I’m making a blunder?

definitions.text: With this I’m making a blunder?

indicators.note: a blunder is a mess-up, so the preceding letters are botched into a different order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A golfer or batsman asks whether this shot is going to be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: a bad stroke is how a player blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishit is a badly struck shot in a ball game, a clumsy error with bat, club or racket.

clue.text: See 24
With pressure on, Paul being sick unfortunately – giving Ted Talks etc?

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events goes wrong, so the letters go awry into a new arrangement

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Under pressure, the setter Paul is taken ill before addressing an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With pressure on' adds P to the letters being rearranged. Paul is this puzzle's setter, so the surface is self-mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: TED Talks are short lectures delivered to an audience, examples of addressing a crowd from a stage.

clue.text: Sponsor picked up for a quid, say?

indicators.note: picked up means heard or caught by the ear, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a backer is a sponsor, and in a non-rhotic British accent the two words are said the same

explanation.surface: Asking whether a sponsor might be bought cheaply, for a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: A quid is British slang for a pound, but here it is a chewing lump of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacca is informal British slang for tobacco, and a quid is a wad of it for chewing, hence the 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: A report about damaged tin foil

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are reshaped
about means around, so the preceding pieces wrap round what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged
a thesis is a written dissertation or report

explanation.surface: A report about some tin foil that has been damaged, perhaps a kitchen mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' looks like the metal sheet; here it means a contrast.
explanation.definitionFit: A foil is a person or thing that sets off another by contrast, and an exact opposite serves that role.

clue.text: One ripping up verses, perhaps, after first found in Christmas cracker?

indicators.note: the first found in a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken
one piece coming after another is placed behind it

blocks.note: first letter of Christmas
an ode is a poem, made of verses
one who rips things up breaks them

explanation.surface: Someone tearing up the paper mottoes or rhymes found inside a Christmas cracker.
explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is the British party favour pulled apart with a bang, holding a joke or rhyme; here 'cracker' is someone who cracks ciphers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cracks secret ciphers is a code-cracker, so the question mark lets cracker stand for that person.
